docs.task: How the server's session endpoints are defined and guarded, and how they read from the workspace db.

asks: How the server's session endpoints are defined
How they read from the workspace db

data_flow.step: Browser calls `GET /api/sessions/{id}/events?after=N` (web client `request<StoredEvent[]>`). The request first passes the single middleware layer.

`guard` computes `api = path.starts_with("/api/") || path == "/ws"`, filters the `Host` header through `app.auth.allowed_host` (421 MISDIRECTED_REQUEST when not allowed), and on a loopback-IP host redirects pages or refuses the API with 421 (`private_redirect`).

`refusal` runs for `/api` paths: `allowed_origin(Origin)` must pass; `Sec-Fetch-Site` of `cross-site` or `same-site` is refused; `Sec-Fetch-Dest` must be absent or one of `empty`, `websocket`, `document`; any failure gives 403 'This origin is not allowed.'. Then, for every path except `/api/auth/exchange`, the session cookie is read with `cookie_value` and validated with `check_cookie`; failure gives 401 'Sign in with the URL the ostra command printed.' and an info log.

`check_cookie` hashes the cookie, uses an in-memory cache entry younger than RECHECK, otherwise reads the sign-in record from the registry kv store, deletes expired ones, and refreshes `last_seen` with `kv_replace`.
After the request passes, `secure_headers` adds the CSP, `nosniff`, `no-referrer`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, and, for API paths, `Cache-Control: no-store` to the response, including refusals.

Axum dispatches to `session_events`. It builds `SessionId::from(id)` and calls `ws_of_session`, which iterates `App::all_workspaces()` and returns the first `WorkspaceRt` whose `db.get_session(id)` is Some, else 404 'No session {id}.'.

The handler reads straight from the db (not the engine's cached fold): `w.db.events_after(&sid, q.after.unwrap_or(0))`, which runs `Events::after` under the Db mutex: `SELECT seq, at, payload FROM events WHERE session_id = ?1 AND seq > ?2 ORDER BY seq`, and decodes `payload` JSON into `SessionEvent`. The Vec<StoredEvent> is returned as JSON.

Contrast, `GET /api/sessions/{id}`: `w.engine.detail(&sid)` calls `Engine::state`, which calls `Inner::load`. On first touch `load` checks `db.get_session`, calls `db.events(id)` (events_after with 0), runs `SessionState::fold`, and caches the `Live` state in `Inner.sessions`. `view::detail` then combines the folded state with `db.list_executions`.
Writes go the other way: `Inner::append` stores via `WorkspaceDb::append_event` (assigns next seq in a transaction and touches sessions.updated_at), folds, broadcasts, and wakes the driver.

patterns.description: Session ids carry no workspace, so every /api/sessions/{id}/* handler calls `ws_of_session`, which scans `app.all_workspaces()` and returns the first whose `db.get_session(id)` is `Some`. Reads that need folded state go through `w.engine`; raw reads go through `w.db`. Gate, execution, and decision handlers use the same pattern with `ws_of_gate`, `ws_of_execution`, `ws_of_decision`. Workspace-scoped routes (`/api/workspaces/{ws}/sessions`) use `ws(&app, &id)` instead, which looks up the map directly. Handlers that start work take `start_work(&w).await?` first.
patterns.name: Session handler: resolve owning workspace by probing each workspace db, then call the engine or the db

patterns.description: Every route is a `.route(path, method(handler))` on one `axum::Router` built in `router()`. Paths use axum's `{param}` syntax. patterns.description: Handlers return `Res<T> = Result<Json<T>, ApiErr>`. `From<EngineError>` maps NotFound to 404, Invalid and Ended to 409, Store to 500. `From<StoreError>` maps every store error to 500, so a missing session through `?` on a db call is a 500 unless the handler first resolved the session with `ws_of_session` (404).

patterns.description: Each table has a crate-private repository struct wrapping `&Connection` that holds its SQL and row mapping (`Events`, `Sessions`, ...). `WorkspaceDb` methods call `self.db.run(|c| Repo(c).method(..))` for single statements and `self.db.transaction(..)` (BEGIN IMMEDIATE) for multi-statement writes. `append_event` appends the event and touches `sessions.updated_at` in one transaction. Reads in `Events::after` use `query_all` with `RowExt::time` and `RowExt::json` to decode `at` and `payload`.

submit.findings_summary: Session routes are registered in `router()` in crates/ostra-server/src/api.rs, and a single `guard` middleware wraps the whole router. It checks the Host allowlist, the Origin, and the Sec-Fetch headers, then the signed-in cookie (every path except /api/auth/exchange), and it adds the security headers. A session id carries no workspace, so handlers call `ws_of_session`, which probes every open workspace db with `get_session`. `GET /api/sessions/{id}/events` reads `WorkspaceDb::events_after` directly (SQL in crates/ostra-store/src/workspace/events.rs), while `GET /api/sessions/{id}` goes through `Engine::detail`. That path loads the session once with `Inner::load`, which replays `db.events` into `SessionState::fold`. The only writer is `Inner::append`, via `WorkspaceDb::append_event`. All store access shares one Mutex-guarded rusqlite connection in WAL mode. The events route has no e2e test.

docs.task: How stored events are read from the store and serialized.

asks: How stored events are read from the store

data_flow.step: An event is appended by the engine: `Inner::append` holds the session state lock, calls the store, folds the event into state, and broadcasts an EngineNotice::Event.
The store serializes SessionEvent to JSON (`serde_json::to_value`), inserts a row (session_id, seq, type, payload text, at text) inside an immediate transaction, and returns a StoredEvent.

Read request: a caller invokes `WorkspaceDb::events(session)` (all rows) or `events_after(session, after)` (rows with seq greater than `after`). `Db::run` locks the shared connection for the duration.
`Events::after` runs `SELECT seq, at, payload FROM events WHERE session_id = ?1 AND seq > ?2 ORDER BY seq` through `query_all`, which collects every row into a Vec before returning.

Each row is deserialized: `seq` as i64, `at` through `parse_time` (RFC 3339), and `payload` through `serde_json::from_str` into SessionEvent via the `type` tag. A bad timestamp gives StoreError::Invalid; a bad payload gives StoreError::Json.
Engine consumer: `Inner::load` reads all events once per session, folds them into SessionState, and caches the Live state. `stop_session_offline` does the same read for the CLI stop command.

REST consumer: `GET /api/sessions/{id}/events?after=N` returns `Json<Vec<StoredEvent>>`. Each element serializes as `{"seq":..,"at":"..Z","event":{"type":"snake_case_name",...fields}}` (chrono serde output for `at`). The web client reads it in `api.events`.

Live consumer: the hub forwards EngineNotice::Event to `route` in ws.rs, which builds ServerMsg::SessionEvent with seq, at, and event, and `send` writes `serde_json::to_string(msg)` as a WebSocket text frame on channel `session:{id}`.

patterns.description: Store read queries use `query_all` with a closure that builds the value from named columns. TEXT columns that hold JSON are read with `r.json(col)`, and times with `r.time(col)`. The events read follows this exactly, so the payload text is deserialized straight into SessionEvent and the `type` column is not read on the way out (it is written only so the column can be inspected or filtered in SQL).

patterns.description: `append` serializes the event to a serde_json::Value first, reads the `type` tag from it for the `type` column, then stores `payload.to_string()` (compact JSON, no trailing newline). The `at` value is produced by `now()` as RFC 3339 UTC with milliseconds and parsed back to build the returned StoredEvent.

patterns.description: API handlers resolve the workspace from the session id, call the store, and return `Res<T>` which axum serializes with serde. The events endpoint returns the full Vec<StoredEvent> as a single JSON array (Content-Type application/json). No handler in the repo streams newline-delimited JSON.

document.problem: Session events are written as one JSON payload per row in the workspace SQLite database and read back through a single query, then deserialized into StoredEvent values. The same StoredEvent type is serialized to JSON for the REST endpoint and, as a ServerMsg frame, for the WebSocket. This document records the exact read and serialization path so a change to how events are read or emitted (for example a different output format) can be placed correctly.

Covers the SQLite events table, the read path in ostra-store, the StoredEvent and SessionEvent serde shapes, and every consumer of that read path (engine load, offline stop, REST, WebSocket). It does not cover the materialized tables, the web client rendering of events, or any export format, because none exists in the repo.
document.title: How stored events are read from the store and serialized

submit.findings_summary: Events live in the workspace.db `events` table (session_id, seq, type, payload JSON text, at RFC 3339 text). The only read query is `Events::after` in crates/ostra-store/src/workspace/events.rs. `WorkspaceDb::events` and `events_after` call it. It collects all matching rows into a Vec<StoredEvent> through `query_all`, using `RowExt::json` and `RowExt::time`. SessionEvent is serde-tagged with `type` in snake_case, and StoredEvent is {seq, at, event}. Consumers are the engine (`Inner::load` and offline stop), the REST endpoint `GET /api/sessions/{id}/events?after=N` (one JSON array), and the WebSocket (`ServerMsg::SessionEvent` frames from ws.rs `route` and `send`). The write side and the docs page that describes the format (docs/architecture/storage.md) are also recorded. The repo has no streaming or line-delimited event output: the only .jsonl uses are harness transcript files.
